mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thus depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the past 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative despite a statistically significant positive correlation (p < 0.05) between the labor indicators in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average indicates expanding domestic demand for goods, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as firms respond with production and investment.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2%
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when INDPRO breaks its moving average threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests deflationary pressures, lowering real earnings and pushing down S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive during CPIAUCSL < 2% periods (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the Russell 2000 price/earnings ratio (not directly observable here, but proxy via GDPC1 demand growth) turns over while FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, it indicates a potential shift from tightening to stability, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of GDPC1 turns positive while FEDFUNDS < 4%
regime_hint: transition from tightening to stable policy
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive during such policy regime transitions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs (implied by UNRATE stability) suggests a healthy labor market, which can fuel consumer spending and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE remains flat
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative despite a high positive correlation (r > 0.6) between PAYEMS spike and subsequent 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 3% indicates disinflation, lowering real interest rates and encouraging risk appetite, which should drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months below 3%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL shows such declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the housing starts (HOUST) fall for two consecutive months while industrial production (INDPRO) remains steady, it signals a shift toward supply-side constraints in the economy, which can lead to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months while INDPRO does not decline
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative during such supply-side imbalances (p < 0.05).
